The current model therefore uses evidence-driven, reversible controls while keeping database truth and ordinary restart recovery entirely separate from optimization state. answer.answer: Prioritize `/in/playerActivity`: keep stale data available and refresh it asynchronously under a lock so foreground requests never run the Redis scan/rebuild. Separately, make the raid page render fast local raid results before Bungie collectible enrichment and avoid the eager duplicate Pantheon fetch.

claims.value: The highest-value non-profile target is the `/in/playerActivity` cache-miss path. Over 7 days, RUM recorded 13,210 calls averaging 3.69 s with p75 1.09 s and p95 12.03 s; APM recorded 23,255 exact `GET /in/playerActivity` spans averaging 1.99 s with p75 2 ms and p95 13.03 s. In the last 24 hours, logs showed 68 foreground rebuilds and 204 shard logs, with shard-scan p95 about 18 s and math p95 about 16 s.

Change `apiPlayerActivity` from foreground rebuild-on-miss to stale-while-revalidate: retain a longer-lived stale value, refresh it in the background every five minutes, and use a single-flight or distributed lock so only one worker performs `memcache.GetPlayerActivity`. Serve stale data while refresh is running or fails, falling back to the established no-data behavior only when no usable value exists. This addresses the code-path problem that the API currently reads the `apiPlayerActivity` cache and makes a web request pay the Redis scan when that cache misses, while `sweeperbot.cachePlayerActivity` writes with a five-minute TTL on the same five-minute cadence.

On `/p/:identifier/raids`, the bottleneck is Bungie collectible/profile enrichment, not local raid SQL or images. `loadLogbookRaidSources` waits for every source, including slow `bungie.GetD2ProfileStats(..., bungie.ProfileWCollectibles)`, before responding; the SPA also eagerly starts a separate Pantheon `ProfileWCollectibles` request before that tab is opened. APM over 24 hours measured `GET /in/logbook/profile/:identifier/raids` at 195 spans, avg 1.81 s, p75 2.33 s, p95 3.77 s, while local `raiddifficultysummaries`, `raidcarries`, and `raidseals` sources were only about 2.7 ms, 6.1 ms, and 0.6 ms respectively. Return the shell and fast local clears/full clears/carries/fastest data first, defer collectible/progress enrichment, and lazy-load Pantheon when selected or share/cache one server-side `ProfileWCollectibles` result.

After the player-activity change, compare exact `GET /in/playerActivity` RUM/APM call volume and avg/p75/p95 with the saved 7-day baselines, and measure foreground rebuild count, shard-scan/math duration, fresh/stale/miss responses, served-stale age, refresh attempts/successes/failures, and lock contention; success means foreground rebuilds approach zero and the roughly 12–13 s p95 tail collapses without availability regressions. After the raid change, compare raids and Pantheon RUM/APM avg/p75/p95, measure time to first real raid cards, Bungie-profile source latency, local-source timing, and `ProfileWCollectibles` calls per raid view; success means local raid cards render before collectible enrichment and an unopened Pantheon tab causes no duplicate Bungie fetch.

answer.answer: The evidence supports a DB-contention incident led by a delayed leaderboard-work wave, not a deploy or restart. Pause new `global_profile_leaderboards` fetches first, allow in-flight work to drain, and then remeasure the named database and session metrics before escalating.

claims.value: On 2026-06-20, production `rhea` was CPU-saturated—idle around `1.5%`, user CPU around `88%`—primarily from MySQL and Cortex DB work: `mysqld` was around `2855%` CPU and `warmind-cortex` around `965%`, versus `warmind-parser` around `108%`. The supported causal story is that a delayed wave of `global_profile_leaderboards` work became active; that job has `MaxConcurrency: 0`, effectively unbounded in gocraft/work terms, while the ops scheduling rule `12h + deterministic_hash(membershipId) % 48h` allows work to arrive later without an overnight code or configuration change. The leaderboard wave plus session fanout increased the cost of DB-backed work until MySQL became the limiting resource. Parser/API/Cortex uptime was about 25 hours with no reset inside the prior 24 hours, so a deploy or restart is not supported as the cause. Because the original live enqueue transcript/count was not recovered, the delayed-wave link is strongly supported by queue shape and known scheduling behavior, not proven from command output.

claims.value: Parser throughput alone is misleading because its rate remained normal—around `85 PGCR/s`, close to the 2026-06-19 same-window `84 PGCR/s`—while the cost and latency of each DB-backed unit rose sharply. Parser transaction duration increased from around `89 ms` to around `318 ms`; parser DB queue waits averaged about `2044 ms` and peaked above `23 s`; and `mysqld` CPU rose from about `674%` to about `2855%`. Concurrently, `session_pgcr_seen` processed around `35/s`, similar to the prior day, but average duration rose from about `40 ms` to about `2.36 s`, while `session_finalize_due` average duration rose from about `1.9 s` to about `99 s`. Thus a matching PGCR rate conceals severe contention and increased unit cost rather than demonstrating healthy capacity.

claims.value: Verified constraint: Update 1 (0.2.x) and a level-0 Base Core with 1,000 capacity; exceeding capacity disables Fire Wave protection. Revised proposal: abandon the monolithic mega-base, build a starter hub whose active aggregate heat remains at or below 1,000 with reserve headroom, and add satellite production cells after measurements or core upgrades. Do not combine a Constructorizer (500 heat) and Facturer (650 heat) under the present core because their 1,150 combined heat already exceeds its entire capacity. Use Ore Excavator v.1 rather than Laser Drills for basic Titanium, Wolfram, and Calcium; reserve Laser Drills for Goethite.

Proposed live-logistics pattern, not verified built state: route each basic-ore excavator into an input buffer, then smelting, then separate block or part buffers; feed downstream production from those protected buffers and route only overflow toward export. Keep a construction-stock floor so exports cannot drain materials needed for expansion or recovery. Exact container quantities, stock-floor thresholds, transport tiers, priority behavior, and backpressure rules remain unset until measured in game. Verified rate anchor: Ore Excavator v.1 produces 60/120/240 items per minute on Impure/Normal/Pure nodes; smelter throughput must be checked when sizing each bank.

Proposed exports: export only measured surplus from finished block and part buffers after the protected construction-stock floor is satisfied; stop or backpressure exports whenever local consumption lowers stock beneath that floor. Exportable products and exact thresholds are not yet verified. Proposed single defense/recovery provision: maintain a protected habitat cache powered by an Interior Power Generator, which the evidence lists at +100 power, 0 heat, and immunity to star waves. Core heat must remain at or below 1,000 so Base Core Fire Wave protection is not disabled.
